questions.q: What are the three properties of the CIA triad as applied to a security NFR?
options: Cost, implementation, administration
Confidentiality, integrity, availability
Classification, isolation, auditing
Compliance, identity, access
questions.explain: The CIA triad breaks security into confidentiality (only authorized people can see data), integrity (data is accurate and untampered), and availability (authorized users can access it when needed).

questions.q: Why does field-level security satisfy a confidentiality requirement more reliably than hiding a field only on a page layout?
options: Hiding a field on a page layout actually deletes the data from the database
Page layouts and field-level security are the exact same mechanism under a different name
Field-level security only works for custom fields, never for standard fields
Field-level security is enforced consistently across the UI, API, and reports, while a page-layout change only hides the field in that one layout and can be bypassed through other access paths
questions.explain: Field-level security is a platform-enforced control that applies everywhere a field could be accessed — UI, API, reports — whereas removing a field from a page layout only affects that layout and leaves the field visible through other access paths like the API or a report.

questions.q: What does Salesforce Shield's Platform Encryption feature add beyond base-platform field-level security?
options: It encrypts specific fields and files at rest under customer-controlled encryption, addressing a confidentiality need beyond controlling who can merely see a field
It replaces the need for profiles and permission sets entirely
It automatically deletes data after a retention period expires
It is required before any Salesforce org can go live in production
questions.explain: Field-level security controls who can see a field's value. Platform Encryption addresses a different confidentiality concern — encrypting the data at rest, under keys the customer controls — which matters even for users or integrations that otherwise have legitimate access.

questions.q: A compliance officer says: "We need to detect anomalous data access, like a user exporting an unusually large number of records." Which Shield feature is purpose-built to satisfy this NFR?
options: Field Audit Trail
Platform Encryption
Event Monitoring
Multi-factor authentication
questions.explain: Event Monitoring captures detailed platform events, including report exports and API activity, into a queryable log and can feed near-real-time transaction security policies — exactly the tooling needed to detect and respond to anomalous access patterns.

questions.q: Why is recommending Salesforce Shield described in this lesson as an architectural judgment call rather than a default best practice?
options: Because Shield is being deprecated by Salesforce and should never be recommended
Because Shield is a separately licensed bundle, and it should be justified by a specific NFR the base platform's security model doesn't already satisfy, not reached for automatically
Because Shield only works in Government Cloud orgs
Because Shield replaces the role hierarchy and sharing rules, making base security configuration unnecessary
questions.explain: Shield carries its own licensing cost, so an architect should recommend it when a specific security NFR actually requires a capability the base platform (role hierarchy, sharing rules, profiles, field-level security, MFA) doesn't already provide — not as a reflexive default.
